neighbours.label: the word right after a modal + 'be' (could be wrong, can be especially, might be so): the complement slot of a hedged or generalising 'be'; the same word after plain 'was/is' stays low
fire: That is how I remember the vote, but I could be wrong on the details.
The museum closes at five, I think, though I may be wrong.
Long drives at night can be especially tiring for new drivers.
These forms can be very confusing if you fill them out in a hurry.
Spring storms in this valley can be especially violent.
The ferry runs every hour, unless I am misremembering, but I could be wrong.
The last mile of the trail can be very steep after rain.
Old wiring like this can be especially dangerous in a damp cellar.
quiet: That is how I remember the vote, and the minutes were wrong on the details.
The museum closes at five, and the sign on the door is wrong.
Long drives at night were tiring for him as a new driver.
These forms are confusing, so take your time when you fill them out.
Spring storms in this valley were violent last year.
The ferry runs every hour, and the timetable on the pier was wrong.
The last mile of the trail is steep and rocky.
Old wiring like this was found in the cellar during the inspection.

notes: Card max is small (4.56): ' wrong' in 'could be wrong', ' especially'/' very'/' so' after 'can be'/'could be'. Probe: 'I could be wrong' 1.247, 'I might be wrong' 0.615, 'can be especially hard' 0.772, 'can be very tricky' 0.366, 'could be a long night' 0.486 (on ' if'), 'I was wrong about' 0.051, 'was wrong, and' 0.022.
